newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's Franco sees 1997 trade gap at $15 bln.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's Franco sees 1997 trade gap at $15 bln.

text.p: Brazil's Central Bank International Affairs Director Gustavo Franco said the trade deficit could hit a record $15 billion in 1997, the O Globo newspaper reported Sunday.
The figure compares with last year's $5 billion trade gap.
Franco said the figure was not causing the government any concern because it was considered to be "compatible with the international scenario", O Globo newspaper said.
"I believe the trade deficit will not really reach this amount, but if it does it will be considered to be normal," Franco was quoted as saying by O Globo.

He said the government was more concerned about dollar flows than monthly trade gap figures because many imports were not paid for in the same year as they were ordered and many exports were paid for in advance, O Globo said.
"From a management poit of view, dollar flows are more important than the imports and exports registered," Franco was quoted as saying.
"Foreign trade creates its own financing and therefore the deficit poses no problem for Brazil."
((--Simona de Logu, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 507 4151))
